title: CtLog::usable_from_ms: None has conflicting documented meanings
description: Option<u64> is the wrong type when None means two different things. Old: PKIX-ppbr.18
close_reason:
Option<u64> replaced with the three-state UsableFrom { At(u64), Unrecorded, Never }, which is what the bead asked for: the contract had three states the caller cares about and Option could express two.

The bug half (ppbr.1) was already fixed — log_window_contains rejects on None, matching the field's docs. What remained was the type. None meant 'never became usable, reject every SCT' while from_google_log_list_json needed 'usable, but the v3 schema records only the current state so there is no usable timestamp' and used Some(0) as a sentinel, documented as such, working only because no timestamp precedes the Unix epoch. Readonly and retired logs now import as Unrecorded rather than as a fabricated epoch, and qualified logs as Never.

Guarded by an_unrecorded_start_is_not_the_same_as_never_usable, which asserts the two give opposite answers across the timestamp range — the assertion that previously could not be written without encoding the Some(0) convention into the test. Verified by mutation: letting Never fall through the window check fails it.

Shipped in pkix-ct 0.3.0 (unpublished).
